description: The public update feed a client reads to learn a release exists. core/feed.js imports this and builds the feed URL and channel names from it; the iOS client mirrors the two values it needs (mobile/Claw/UpdateFeed.swift) proven by a parity test; and the mobile release workflow (.github/workflows/mobile-pipeline.yml) publishes the marker to `pagesPath`, which is the one string that workflow and feedUrl() share. Same idiom as spec/updates.json and spec/naming.json.
why: The feed is a tiny static JSON document, not electron-updater's `.yml` metadata. The `.yml` carries a download URL, a size and a checksum for a file an updater is about to apply; iOS applies nothing, so a marker that named an installer would promise something no iOS build can honour. All the phone needs is the newest version, so that is all this feed carries.

It is on GitHub Pages rather than behind the gateway, because the phone cannot authenticate to a gateway yet (Phase 3) and a public feed is the correct shape regardless: knowing a release exists is not privileged information, and a CDN-served static file needs no auth and no rate-limited API. `pagesPath` is where the mobile release workflow writes it and where feedUrl() reads it, so the two ends cannot drift.

Only `dev` has a feed today, and that is honest about the world rather than a gap: TestFlight is the one distribution channel and every build on it is a dev build. `stable` is named so channelFor() on a future release build can say there is no feed yet rather than guessing a URL for one.
